note: The frozen quiet-host thresholds for the REL-3 qualifying soak. Registered BEFORE the qualifying run was launched and never adjusted afterwards. scripts/rel3-soak-eligibility.mjs reads this file; it does not carry its own copy of these numbers, so the contract and the scorer cannot drift apart. The file's SHA-256 is recorded in the attempt's launch record.

window.note: The measured window is the final four hours of the run, matching the harness's final-window RSS rule (FR-13's four hours).

foreignCores.note: Three gates on the foreign CPU, each catching a different shape of interference: the window mean bounds the TOTAL interference, the nearest-rank p95 catches a recurring workload that occupies a minority of the samples, and the rolling five-minute mean catches a sustained neighbour that a whole-window mean would hide. A one-minute spike survives all three (it contributes 0.20 to a five-minute mean); a twelve-minute one-core neighbour fails the rolling gate; a forty-percent-duty neighbour fails the p95.

coverage.note: The window must hold at least this fraction of the expected samples at the registered cadence. The window's samples are the ones inside the final four hours of the run.

dispositions.note: A breach makes the attempt CONFOUNDED: recorded under its own name as incomplete, never scored, never re-scored. Missing or invalid telemetry has the same disposition — it is never read as a quiet host. A valid host window permits the unchanged memory and other gates to be scored; it does not itself confer a PASS.
